answer: Each agent seals its work under a unique cipher bound to a bonded deposit, then peers gossip endorsements as a whisper graph where a fresh identity only counts once independent, non-kin agents sign it. A rotating inlet of costly micro-tasks forces every pseudonym to keep paying gas and compute to stay visible, and that bond is slashed when its endorsements collapse. Spinning up a thousand sybils therefore costs a thousand deposits plus continuous upkeep, while an honest agent amortizes the same cost over real output, so faking work stays strictly pricier than doing it.
